And at the turn of the year,
which is the year 1572
(of the Greeks),
likewise the Tatars came to Syria, with Kūkā-Ilge Noyan standing at their head,
and he reached as far as Homs, and took captives and slaughtered.
And because the inhabitants of Syria had fled to Aleppo,
that Noyan commanded
that they should all come out,
and that the people of each district and city should sit apart,
and return to their places.
And when they did so,
he killed them all,
and spared only the people of Aleppo alone.
To the rest, however, they said:
"If you were our friends,
you would not have fled from before us."
And when Kūkā-Ilge Noyan had done these things,
he returned from Syria and crossed the Euphrates.
And the Egyptians came again,
and ruled over all Syria.
And in the summer of this year,
Ala al-Din, son of Badr al-Din, lord of Sinjar,
who had fled to the Egyptians,
sent a letter to Malik Salih, his brother, lord of Mosul,
informing him of the strength of the Egyptians,
and that it was expedient for him to leave Mosul for the time being
and go to Bunduqdar,
so that when he should break the Tatars,
he might make him rule not only over Assyria {Athōr},
but also over all the East.
And on one of the days, while a certain man of the nobles of Badr al-Din, named Bar Yūnis, was sitting with Malik Salih,
he stretched his hand under the rug,
and stole from beneath it that dispatch which had come from his brother,
and he arose, went out, and went to his village named Bet Ashiqa in Nineveh.
And after an hour Salih looked for that dispatch and did not find it,
and he knew that Bar Yūnis had taken it.
And he urgently sent two servants to search for him.
And when they came to him,
he knew that evil had befallen him {or: was brewing},
and that if he fell into the hands of Salih, he would perish.
Therefore, he gave gifts to those servants,
and set wine before them and said:
"Eat, drink, and make merry this evening,
and in the morning we will enter Mosul together."
And while they were drinking and became drunk,
Bar Yūnis arose in the night,
and took his men, mounted, and came to Bartelli.
